_comment: A RATCHET, NOT A TARGET. scripts/mutate.js runs a fixed, seeded sample of mutants and this is the number the suite currently catches. CI fails if it drops. It does not have to go up, and chasing 100% is the classic mutation-testing mistake: most of the survivors left are `||` -> `&&` inside defaulting expressions like `a || b`, where the mutant is close to equivalent and a test written to kill it would assert nothing anybody cares about. What the ratchet stops is a change that quietly makes the SUITE weaker — deleting an assertion, loosening a boundary, or replacing a real check with one that cannot fail.
_pool: The number of mutants the sample was drawn from. IT IS PART OF THE BASELINE'S IDENTITY: mutate.js shuffles the whole pool with the seed and takes the first `budget`, so adding or removing a single operator anywhere in scripts/lib/*.js re-rolls WHICH 60 get run, and the recorded count stops describing the same sample. mutate.js warns when this no longer matches.
_why_49: 2026-10-02, measured in CI on 53afe8c (81.7%), up from 29 of the same 269-mutant pool earlier the same day. THIS IS THE DIRECTION THIS NUMBER IS ALLOWED TO MOVE and it is earned, not found: 21 new tests across lib/fieldmap.js (13), lib/season.js and lib/rushing.js (8), every one written against a NAMED survivor from the gate's own list and verified by putting that mutation back and watching it go red. fieldmap.js went from 12 survivors to 0 — it was the thinnest-covered file in the repo by a factor of three and also the one publishing a twelve-cell heatmap, which is the combination its own header warns about. The suite went 481 -> 547 tests over the week.
_the_11_left: match.js 3, weekly.js 2, cadence.js 2, season.js 1, overrides.js 1, rushing.js 1, scoring.js 1. Mostly arithmetic and `||`-inside-defaulting, which is the near-equivalent category this file's first line warns against chasing. TWO ARE PROVABLY UNKILLABLE and say so in the code: rushing.js's `num(v)` empty-string branch is dead because lib/match's parseCSV turns '' into null before a row arrives, and scoring.js's week-sort comparator cannot change a result whose keys are integer-like and already iterate in order. Do not spend an afternoon on either.
